nonModelAttribution.method: Union-of-intervals attribution of the agent wall clock, computed from the same frozen evidence the per-call measurement uses (model-request.startedAtMs and the matching closure's durationMs), by .tmp/fh-local-20260924/non-model-attribution.mjs. Model-busy is the union of every call interval, because calls can overlap (a subagent's requests are separate runs and a sum can exceed the wall clock); non-model time is wall clock minus that union, and it decomposes into head (agent start to first call), the gaps between calls (tool execution plus prompt assembly), and the tail (after the last call ends). The per-call table above divides a SUM by the wall clock, so it over- or under-states the model share whenever calls overlap; the numbers below are the decomposition.
nonModelAttribution.correction: The Chinese record for part A states that dna-insert was 'the first cell in this repository whose non-model time approaches half the wall clock (847s)'. That reading is wrong and is corrected here: the 847s is not tool or process time. Union attribution puts dna-insert's model-busy time at 1791s of its 1835s wall clock (98%), with 44s (2%) non-model, of which 34.9s is the post-kill tail; its inter-call gaps sum to 9s (median 0.0s, max 4.0s). The 847s is a single model call that stayed in flight: the last request started at 992.9s and was never answered before the attempt was killed at its 1800s budget, so it was in flight for about 807s. The CLI's own per-call ceiling is modelTimeoutMs=840000 (840s), which is longer than the budget that remained, so the agent budget killed the attempt while one slow call was still outstanding. dna-insert is therefore a model-latency budget outcome, exactly like the other two budget cells, and not a tool-wait one.

datacurve/meriyah-explicit-resource-decl.note: 2 runs and overlapping call intervals: this attempt used a subagent, which is why the per-call sum exceeds the wall clock

previousBatchRecomputed.note: The beta.36 batch (run 36171961895, part B) was recomputed with the same union method so the two batches are read on one basis. Its Chinese record's model-share column is a sum and is superseded by these numbers for the cells it lists.

nonModelAttribution.finding: Across the 17 cells measured with this method (11 in this batch, 6 in the beta.36 part B), time with a model call in flight is 67-98% of the whole agent wall clock, and the residual is dominated by a fixed post-kill tail of 22-160s plus inter-call gaps whose median is 0.0s. Harness-side time (tool execution, prompt assembly, agent startup) is therefore of order seconds to a couple of minutes per cell, while single model calls reach 58.9s to 578.1s and one call held in flight for 807s. Any harness-side optimisation is bounded by that residual: even setting it to zero leaves every budget-exhausted cell short, because in each of them the model-busy time alone already equals 91-98% of the wall clock. What remains unproven, and is being measured separately by the full-corpus max-effort run, is whether the remaining failures are model capability or model latency: the two chronic 900s timeouts are killed mid-iteration, so their verdicts bound capability and speed together and are not clean capability reads.
nonModelAttribution.tailComposition: UNVERIFIED: the tail (wall clock minus the last call's end) is measured, not attributed; it plausibly contains the agent's own finalisation, shutdown and harness teardown, but no artifact separates those.
